headline: S&P 500 barely held flat Friday while the Nasdaq fell 0.64% as chip-sector selling and Middle East oil risk capped a recovery from Thursday's 500-point Dow drop.
stance: Cautious into the Fed. Oil pulling back from $100+ gives equities a modest overnight bid — S&P futures are up ~0.1% and Nasdaq-100 futures ~0.2% in pre-market — but the FOMC meets in four days with market-implied hike odds now near 38%, up from 11% a week ago. Real rates at 2.43% and a 10-year yield at 4.69% (both prior cash close) are already a stiff headwind for long-duration tech. The Iran conflict's pressure on energy prices remains the single biggest macro swing factor this week.

news.head: Iran/Hormuz oil risk eases slightly overnight
news.body: Brent crude slipped to a pre-market level near $96.18/bbl (prior cash close $98.38) and WTI to roughly $88.62/bbl (prior cash close $90.47) after Iran-peace-talk hopes briefly re-emerged, though Secretary of State Rubio said Iran is 'not serious about talks.'

news.head: Fed hike odds near 38% ahead of Jul 29 FOMC
news.body: Fed funds futures now price roughly a 38% chance the Fed raises rates at Wednesday's meeting — up from just 11% two weeks ago — driven by oil-fueled inflation and May PCE running at 4.1%, more than double the 2% target.

news.head: Tech capex fears weighed on Nasdaq last week
news.body: The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF fell more than 5% on the week as investors worried AI data-center spending was consuming cash flow faster than it was generating returns, even as Intel beat earnings expectations.

news.head: Uber -4.3% Friday on Waymo split
news.body: Uber shed roughly 4.3% Friday — wiping ~$6.1bn in market cap — after reports that Waymo is considering withdrawing from their robotaxi partnership.

news.head: PMI flash: services up, manufacturing slows, prices hot
news.body: July flash PMIs showed US services activity strengthening while manufacturing growth slowed and price pressures intensified, adding to the stagflationary narrative that is keeping yields elevated.

news.head: Paramount hits 52-week low after Warner deal blocked
news.body: Paramount closed at $8.21, touching its 52-week low of $8.17, after a court halted its proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

implications: The overnight oil pullback is welcome but not decisive — Brent is still near multi-year highs (prior cash close $98.38/bbl, 93.8th percentile of its 3-year range) and one Strait of Hormuz headline could reverse it instantly.

A 38% market-implied probability of a July Fed hike means the FOMC on Wednesday is a genuine coin-flip risk event, not a rubber-stamp; any hawkish surprise would likely hit long-duration tech and rate-sensitive names hard.

Real rates at 2.43% combined with a CAPE ratio of 40.46 leave equities with very little cushion — the equity risk premium is negative at -2%, meaning bonds are offering more expected return than stocks on a risk-adjusted basis.

Positioning: Speculators are almost entirely out of Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile of a 3-year range — a contrarian floor), and WTI crude futures specs are at the 6th percentile (also a contrarian floor despite high spot prices). Copper specs are at the 91st percentile — speculators are heavily positioned long, a contrarian warning. In rates, 2-year Treasury specs are at the 85th percentile — also an extended long and a contrarian warning for a bond rally.

watch.head: FOMC Wed Jul 29 — hold or hike?
watch.body: The Fed announces at 2pm ET Wednesday; with ~38% hike odds priced, any move or notably hawkish language from Chair Warsh (who gives minimal forward guidance) could jolt rates and equities simultaneously.

watch.head: Oil — Strait of Hormuz headlines
watch.body: Brent is in overnight pre-market retreat but any new Houthi tanker attack or Hormuz closure headline could push it back above $100 and re-price the entire hike-odds curve higher within hours.

watch.head: 10-year yield — 5% test?
watch.body: The 10-year closed at 4.69% (prior cash close) after a four-session rally to its highest since January 2025; analysts note 5% is a plausible next target if oil re-accelerates or the Fed surprises hawkish.

watch.head: Big tech earnings this week
watch.body: Amazon and Apple both report this week (Amazon Wednesday, Apple Friday), giving the market a chance to either confirm or dismiss AI-capex spending fears that crushed Magnificent Seven names last week.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: 4.69% (prior cash close), at its highest since January 2025 after a four-session climb driven by oil-inflation fears; the 2-year sits at 4.33% (prior cash close), leaving the 2s10s curve at +36 bps — still positive but slim.
10-year breakeven inflation (the bond market's inflation forecast) is at 2.26% (prior cash close), meaning real rates are a restrictive 2.43% — genuine headwind for growth assets.
Term premium — the extra yield investors demand for holding long-term bonds — stands at 77.9 bps, reflecting genuine fiscal and inflation uncertainty rather than purely rate expectations.
Fed funds futures price ~38% odds of a 25 bp hike at the July 29 FOMC, up from ~11% two weeks ago; September hike odds are near 82% — markets are pricing two hikes as the base case for 2026.
July flash PMI showed services expanding but manufacturing slowing with intensifying price pressures — a stagflationary mix that complicates the Fed's calculus.
DXY (dollar index): 101.46 (prior cash close); USD/JPY: 163.791 (prior cash close) — yen is at a 3-year extreme (99.9th percentile), with the BOJ under pressure to hike and squeeze carry trades.
sections.positioning: In rates, speculative positioning on 3-month SOFR is at the 3rd percentile of its 3-year range — specs are nearly entirely out (an extended short), which is a contrarian-bullish lean for short rates (i.e., a signal rates could fall). Conversely, 2-year Treasury specs are at the 85th percentile — an extended long, a contrarian warning that the bond-bull trade is overloaded.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 prior cash close: 7,411.98; Nasdaq Composite prior cash close: 24,975.82 (down 0.64% Friday); Dow prior cash close: 51,947.25 (up 0.46% as Apple's 3.5% jump lifted blue chips).
S&P 500 futures: ~+0.1% pre-market; Nasdaq-100 futures: ~+0.2% pre-market — modest overnight relief as oil retreats.
Only 58.4% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average, and 41.6% of Nasdaq-100 stocks are above theirs — the index-level recovery is not broadly supported by the average stock.
VIX (fear gauge): 18.58 (prior cash close) — moderate, not panicked; SKEW at 147.3 signals investors are paying up for protection against a sharp left-tail move (a crash hedge).
Tesla shed roughly 19% on the week after a record ~$214.5bn single-day market-cap loss Thursday on AI-capex concerns; the Magnificent Seven ETF fell more than 5% on the week.
CAPE (cyclically adjusted P/E) at 40.46 and a negative equity risk premium of -2% signal that stocks are priced for perfection at a moment when rates are rising and inflation is re-accelerating.
sections.positioning: Russell 2000 futures specs are at the 2nd percentile of their 3-year net-position range — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor for small-caps. This diverges sharply from commercial hedger positioning, adding a squeeze-risk dimension.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — company insiders have been buying (1 insider rule fired); stock trades above its 200-day moving average with a fresh signal; low short interest (1.8 days to cover) limits squeeze risk but also means any institutional selling is unimpeded.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield spreads: 277 bps (as of Jul 23) — the gap extra yield junk-bond investors demand over safe Treasuries; investment-grade spreads at 79 bps. Neither is blowing out, suggesting credit markets are not yet pricing a recession.
FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS spreads (measures of stress in short-term bank funding) are both just 1 bp — essentially zero, meaning interbank funding is orderly with no sign of a liquidity crunch.
Commercial paper funding spread (how much extra it costs companies to borrow for 30-90 days): 18 bps — benign; no funding-market stress visible.

Bank reserves: $3,062bn (as of Jul 22) — ample; the Fed's overnight reverse repo facility (RRP) is nearly drained at $0.7bn, meaning almost all excess cash has left the Fed's parking lot and is circulating in markets.
M2 money supply growing at 5.58% year-over-year (as of May) — above trend, consistent with inflation staying elevated even before the oil shock.
Bank credit expanding at 6.4% year-over-year (as of Jul 15); syndicated loan yields at 7.19% — lending conditions are tightening in cost but not in availability per the SLOOS (loan officer survey).

single_name.note: Jefferies Financial Group (JEF) — company insiders have been buying (1 insider rule fired); stock trades above its 200-day moving average with a fresh, high-conviction signal (score 5/5); short interest is light at 1.2 days to cover, so no squeeze risk — this is a clean insider-buying setup in a broker-dealer that benefits from rising rates and deal activity.
